title: KC gene set research methods
bodyHtml:
The Gene Set Analysis workflow infers phenotypes, additional genes, and mechanisms that may be related to a list of genes (gene set). In this portal, gene sets are derived from: one of six CFDE programs (GlyGen, GTEx, IDG, IMPC/ KOMP2, LINCS, or MoTrPAC); intersections between two of these CFDE programs; or Differential Expression Analysis of CFDE data performed by the Knowledge Center. Visit the CFDE Workbench for more information about CFDE-derived gene sets. Phenotypes are derived from GWAS results in the NHGRI Association to Function Knowledge Portal (A2FKP); visit the A2FKP for more information about GWAS datasets.

Relationships between phenotypes and gene sets were computed using a novel method, PIGEAN (Priors Inferred from GEne ANnotations), employed by A2FKP and the Common Metabolic Diseases Knowledge Portal (CMDKP). PIGEAN is a Bayesian method that jointly models the probability that each gene is involved in a phenotype of interest, given the gene sets that contain the gene (indirect evidence of involvement in a trait) and the GWAS genetic association statistics for variants near the gene (direct evidence of involvement in a trait).

We applied PIGEAN to each of the traits in the A2FKP, in each case fitting a model using all CFDE gene sets, intersections of CFDE gene sets, and (to increase power) gene sets from the Mouse Genome Informatics database (>11,000 mouse model phenotypes) and MSigDB (pathway analyses). The result of each run is (a) for each gene set, estimates of the effect of the gene set on the probability that genes in the gene set are involved in disease, expressed in units of log-odds increase; and (b) for each gene, estimates of the probability that the gene is involved in disease, expressed in units of log-odds increase relative to the baseline probability 5%. Gene set effects are available either for the gene set in isolation (marginal) or within the joint model (joint), and gene probabilities are available either in total (combined), given only GWAS associations for the gene (direct), and given only gene sets the gene is in (indirect). See our webinar for more details on PIGEAN. Details on an earlier version of the method for gene direct evidence have been published previously (Dornbos et al., 2022).

For the genes within each gene set, direct genetic support scores represent the log of the Human Genetic Evidence (HuGE) scores (Dornbos et al., 2022), which quantify the genetic support for involvement of a gene in one of ~1,190 traits on the Association to Function Knowledge Portal. Combined genetic support is composed of direct support (from GWAS associations near the gene) and indirect support (membership in gene sets with genetic support), expressed as log-odds of probability. Consider the following thresholds for interpreting combined genetic support scores:

  • 1: nominally significant
  • 2: strongly suggestive (i.e., indicative that a gene is in a locus but not yet genome-wide significant)
  • 3: very strong (>50% probability that a gene is involved in the phenotype; similar to nearest gene to a GWAS signal)

See the HuGE Calculator documentation for more details.
